# Closed superclass visibility parameter bridges

A public child closes three recursive and dependent parameters of a package
abstract parent. Its compiler-generated visibility bridge forwards an erased
interface input without a cast. The parent extends a separate plain class.
Source and SDK layouts keep the same original class and method contracts.

The frozen observer exercises six routes, a future override and twelve modes,
twice per fresh JVM. It distinguishes the original uncast visibility bridge
from a future specialization bridge, and checks input and receiver identity,
null timing, callback counts, partial writes and exact checked, runtime and
Error propagation. Independent wrong programs qualify those observations.
Same-Code Signature controls retain their exact class or method annotation.

Every emitted Java unit compiles. Independent classfile inventories compare all
original declarations, Code roles, access, Signature, Exceptions and parameters.
Normalized original and rebuilt bridge bytecodes must match exactly, including
the superclass target, loads, absence of casts and return. The report explicitly
identifies that compiler-regenerated bridge as a source projection.
The original-entry observer admits only the existing private generic throw
helper's exact contract. Extra runtime entries and a same-name helper with the
wrong generic declaration are independently rejected.
